paper.title: Unreliable Multi-Armed Bandits: A Novel Approach to Recommendation Systems

unmapped: The learner does not choose arms directly: an unreliable intermediate visits arms by following an irreducible aperiodic Markov chain with transition matrix P; the learner can only perturb P by a pre-fixed amount delta towards a chosen state
The learner knows the transition matrix P and the perturbation size delta
Regret is measured against always playing the optimal arm (mu_star), which is generally unreachable, so regret is linear
settings.definition_quote: Let an unreliable intermediate $I$ visit different arms by traversing an irreducible and aperiodic Markov chain with state space $S$ and a transition probability matrix $P = [p_{i,j}]_{|S| \times |S|}$. ... Let $\delta$ be known as the perturbation variable. ... $C_{T} = \sum_{j = 1}^{T} \Delta_{i} = T\mu^{*} - \sum_{j = 1}^{T}r_{j}$.

symbols.mu_tilde: sum of arm means weighted by the stationary distribution of the transition matrix after applying the optimal perturbation policy pi^{delta*}

conditions: for any perturbation policy pi in Pi
proof assumes the perturbed Markov chain has attained its stationary distribution

source.quote: For any $\pi \in \mathbf{\Pi}$, the $C_{T}$ can be lower bounded (in expectation) as, \mathbf{E}\left(C_{T}\right) \geq T\left( \mu^{*} - \Tilde{\mu}\right). where $\Tilde{\mu}$ is the sum of the means of each the underlying distribution of each arm, weighted by the stationary probability distribution of the transition probability matrix after $\pi^{\delta^{*}}$ policy is applied on the Markov Chain

results.notes: Linear regret lower bound due to limited control over arm pulls. The proof is only given under stationarity; authors claim it holds in order otherwise. Theorem 1 (optimality of pi^{delta*} with known means) is not a bound and is not recorded. No regret guarantee is proved for P^2EE (simulations only).
